- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >7% from prior day); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; force a mean-reversion correction toward 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model shows >2% deviation from true outcome in first 5 days, reduce forecast slope (flatten trend) for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.33), model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 10-day smoothing filter to dampen noise.
